correct_diagnosis: Adrenal tuberculosis causing primary adrenal insufficiency

published_final_diagnosis.label: Adrenal tuberculosis causing primary adrenal insufficiency

source_treatment.description: Hydrocortisone acetate 20 mg daily with adjustments
Isoniazid 300 mg daily, rifapentine 450 mg twice weekly, ethambutol 750 mg daily, levofloxacin 500 mg daily as reported

source_disposition.outcome: Five follow-up visits showed clinical and hormonal improvement.

key_guideline_decisions.note: See docs/guideline_sources.yaml; applicability and alternative care require clinician review.

distractors: Calcified adrenal masses raise malignancy or old granulomatous disease; no constitutional TB symptoms.
critical_safety_points: Recognize primary adrenal insufficiency and risk of adrenal crisis under stress.
Do not assume negative acid-fast stain excludes tuberculosis.
Antituberculous regimen in source is descriptive; independent guideline review is needed before rating as standard.
source_uncertainties: Unspecified dose, timing or normal findings were not inferred.
Published management is descriptive and requires separate normative review.
No explicit ward admission or unit is documented. The report does not describe biochemical exclusion of pheochromocytoma before biopsy.

critical_diagnoses_to_not_miss: Primary adrenal insufficiency with risk of adrenal crisis
